Hi [~accountid:712020:ab95f96b-73f1-4bb8-a5fd-5178ef3f1339] I understand that following very good results with a pilot with the feature “[Driver Queue Optimiser|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PRODWIKI/pages/4247815957/Driver+Queue+Optimizer]” in Portugal, you would like to substitute the feature “Driver Prioritization” by this new feature.

As a summary IMO:

a) in terms of reclassification risk, a substitution of the “Driver Prioritization” by the “Driver Queue Optimiser” would appear not to lead to changes since in both cases we estimate that these features based on acceptance rate decrease our chances to defend the model in court by 40%. These features would appear equally potentially detrimental to Bolt, but it has been a business decision to have them to counterbalance operational changes in bookings.

b) It seems no update of t&c would be needed

c) privacy review needs to be confirmed by privacy team

*RECLASSIFICATION POINT OF VIEW*

One of the reclassification criteria of platform workers in Portugal is the following: “…presume-se a existência de contrato de trabalho quando, na relação entre o prestador de atividade e a plataforma digital se verifiquem algumas das seguintes características:… e) A plataforma digital exerce poderes laborais sobre o prestador de atividade, nomeadamente o *poder disciplinar*, incluindo a *exclusão de futuras atividades* na plataforma através de desativação da conta”. Accordingly, all automatic or statistical blocking (linked to Driver Score & Acceptance Rate) were removed in 2023 (only blockings related to compliance, safety and fraud remain). 

To counterbalance the negative impacts for the business of removing the automatic and statistical blocking the “Driver Prioritization” feature was introduced. The aim was to influence drivers’ behaviour from a positive perspective, i.e. rides are offered in priority to drivers who meet some criteria, including  Driver Score and Acceptance Rate. The “Driver Prioritization” feature presents a risk when it comes to potentially meeting one of several reclassification criteria under the PT law.  However *it was a business decision made to mitigate the negative impact for the business of removing blocking based on Driver Score.*

The new feature “Driver Queue Optimiser” predicts rejections and cancellations for a given order, removing drivers with low predicted finish rates from the matching list. Acceptance Rate is part of the parameters for such prediction. It seems that drivers would not be blocked from the platform based on Acceptance Rate, but the aim is to direct drivers by rewarding the ones with lower rejections and cancellations. In this sense the new feature would still be a concern from a reclassification point of view, but it would appear to me that we would not be materially worst with the “Driver Queue Optimiser” when compared with the “Driver Prioritisation” feature which would appear to entail a similar risk from a reclassification perspective. 

We estimate that dispatch tools based on acceptance rate criteria (such as Prioritisation and Driver Queue Optimiser) *decreases our chances to defend the model in court by 40%*. The confidence level for these features is high.

*TERMS AND CONDITIONS*

These features regarding prioritisation dispatch logic would not appear to trigger a need to update the terms and conditions, since they do not affect the transport agreement. However, I do not have clarity regarding the privacy assessment done concerning these features, which we need to clarify with the privacy team.

Hi *Jiří*, 
You can follow these steps on KB:

[+https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/9406080396178#user-cannot-reserve-a-vehicle-or-order-a-trip-due-to-negative-bolt-balance+|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/9406080396178#user-cannot-reserve-a-vehicle-or-order-a-trip-due-to-negative-bolt-balance]

*The user cannot reserve a vehicle or order a trip due to a negative Bolt Balance*

If the user has a negative Bolt Balance and travels to a country with a different currency, they won't be able to view their balance on the app anymore. Therefore, they won't be able to add funds to it or clear the debt. To resolve this issue, follow the steps outlined below:

*Step 1: Confirm charge details*

* Open User Balance > [+Transaction history+|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/user-balance/trxHistory] in Admin Panel
* Confirm there’s been a charge that caused a negative balance
* Look for a Booking that has: 💳 failed 🟢success
* Open the ride that caused the charge and check the date

*Step 2: Verify the cause*

* Open the Fraud > Calculations > [+User page+|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/fraud/userCalculationResults]
* Look for a decision REJECT TOP UP
** To ensure that the user cannot use the app because of debt, check for rows created on the same day or within one day.
* Is there a REJECT TOP UP decision?
** If yes, refund the trip that caused the debt to the user’s Bolt Balance
** If not, don’t refund the trip; advise the user they can use the app.

If you need any further information, let me know.
 Best regards,

Hi Marina,

Thanks for reaching out.

We have had these fraud price reviews for almost two years, and the process has been the same from the beginning for these types of rides. For these suspicious journeys, we do not check whether the trip happened. That is not our main point. We review if the journey, all its changes and destinations have been approved by Bolt. Bolt acts as the mediator of these services; therefore, all changes must be confirmed through the app to drive. 

We also run checks on risky users attempting to change or update their trips. If we see fraud indicators, we may refuse an update, which also happened in this order. How should the driver handle these situations?

* If the customer refuses to update their trip, it should be finished. The driver should not drive extra distances without our permission. The message should be clear -> follow the app, and if it does not allow it, don’t continue.
* If customers want to extend or change their trip, the driver can advise them to update their trip info; otherwise, they can’t continue.
* If the customer has trouble updating their destination, the rider can place a new order with updated information. You can check this KB article related to the topic: [https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/7643088163474|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/7643088163474].

The price review itself didn't change anything in terms of what would've been charged. The total price would be charged if we hadn't flagged it. The difference in the process is that we expedite the refund when the payment fails instead of refunding later through our other checks. You can compensate the driver for the commission paid, but we strongly recommend never considering the trip itself in these cases. Driver has to be educated that we can't be liable for the customer's wishes that are happening inside the car without approval in the App.

If the user has a negative Bolt Balance and travels to a country with a different currency, they won't be able to view their balance on the app anymore. Therefore, they won't be able to add funds to it or clear the debt. To resolve this issue, follow the steps outlined below:

*Step 1: Confirm charge details*

* Open User Balance > [+Transaction history+|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/user-balance/trxHistory] in Admin Panel
* Confirm there’s been a charge that caused a negative balance
* Look for a Booking that has: 💳 failed 🟢success
* Open the ride that caused the charge and check the date

*Step 2: Verify the cause*

* Open the Fraud > Calculations > [+User page+|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/fraud/userCalculationResults]
* Look for a decision REJECT TOP UP
** To ensure that the user cannot use the app because of debt, check for rows created on the same day or within one day.
* Is there a REJECT TOP UP decision?
** If yes, refund the trip that caused the debt to the user’s Bolt Balance
** If not, don’t refund the trip; advise the user they can use the app.

Updated query for custom area with a buffer around it.



{noformat}with poly as (
	select
		cpa.id,
		cpa.name,
		cpa.city_id,
		city.name as city_name,
		try(ST_Polygon(concat(
			'POLYGON((',
			array_join(
				transform(
					split(snap_polygon, ','),
					e -> array_join(reverse(split(e, ' ')), ' ')
				),
				','
			),
			'))'
		))) as poly
	from ng_public.smart_pickups_area as cpa
	inner join ng_public.admin_system_city as city
		on cpa.city_id = city.id
	where cpa.city_id = 320
),
from_orders as (
	select
		cpa.id as cpa_id,
		date_trunc('month', co.created) as month,
		ST_Intersects(ST_Point(co.lng, co.lat), ST_Buffer(cpa.poly, 0.0003)) is_in_cpa,
		(first_ride.user_id IS NOT NULL) as is_first_ride
	FROM ng_public.company_order as co
	INNER JOIN ng_public.company_order_try as cot
		ON co.id = cot.order_id 
			and co.city_id = cot.city_id
			and cot.state = 'finished'
			and cot.retry_to_try is null
			and cot.created_date between DATE '2023-01-01' and DATE '2023-12-31'
	LEFT JOIN ng_public.etl_first_finished_ride_for_user as first_ride
		on first_ride.order_id = co.id
			AND first_ride.city_id = co.city_id
			and first_ride.created_date between DATE '2023-01-01' and DATE '2023-12-31'
	inner join poly as cpa
		on co.city_id = cpa.city_id
		and cpa.poly is not null
	WHERE
		co.created_date between DATE '2023-01-01' and DATE '2023-12-31'
		and co.state = 'finished'
),
to_orders as (
	select
		cpa.id as cpa_id,
		date_trunc('month', co.created) as month,
		ST_Intersects(ST_Point(cotrl.lng, cotrl.lat), ST_Buffer(cpa.poly, 0.0003)) as is_in_cpa,
		(first_ride.user_id IS NOT NULL) as is_first_ride
	FROM ng_public.company_order as co
	INNER JOIN ng_public.company_order_try as cot
		ON co.id = cot.order_id 
			and co.city_id = cot.city_id
			and cot.state = 'finished'
			and cot.retry_to_try is null
			and cot.created_date between DATE '2023-01-01' and DATE '2023-12-31'
	inner join ng_public.company_order_try_route_log AS cotrl
		on cotrl.city_id = co.city_id
			and cotrl.order_try_id = cot.id
			and cotrl.order_try_state = 'driving_with_client'
			and cotrl.stop_type = 'arrival'
			and cotrl.created_date between DATE '2023-01-01' and DATE '2023-12-31'
	LEFT JOIN ng_public.etl_first_finished_ride_for_user as first_ride
		on first_ride.order_id = co.id
			AND first_ride.city_id = co.city_id
			and first_ride.created_date between DATE '2023-01-01' and DATE '2023-12-31'
	inner join poly as cpa
		on co.city_id = cpa.city_id
		and cpa.poly is not null
	WHERE
		co.created_date between DATE '2023-01-01' and DATE '2023-12-31'
		and co.state = 'finished'
),
from_orders_agg as (
	select
		cpa_id,
		month,
		count(*) as orders,
		sum(case when is_first_ride then 1 end) as first_time_orders
	from from_orders
	where is_in_cpa
	group by 1,2
),
to_orders_agg as (
	select
		cpa_id,
		month,
		count(*) as orders,
		sum(case when is_first_ride then 1 end) as first_time_orders
	from to_orders
	where is_in_cpa
	group by 1,2
)
select
	cpa.city_id as city_id,
	cpa.city_name as city_name,
	cpa.id as cpa_id,
	cpa.name as cpa_name,
	f.month as month,
	coalesce(f.first_time_orders, 0) as from_first_time_orders,
	coalesce(t.first_time_orders, 0) as to_first_time_orders,
	coalesce(f.orders, 0) as from_orders,
	coalesce(t.orders, 0) as to_orders
from from_orders_agg as f
left join to_orders_agg as t
	on f.month = t.month
		and f.cpa_id = t.cpa_id
inner join poly as cpa
	on cpa.id = f.cpa_id
order by city_id, cpa_id, month;{noformat}

Hi [~accountid:624407b9f3824d006a57cd8a] 

As per DL 28/2019, that establishes the regime for invoice storage and retention, all invoices can be kept on a virtual/electronic archive. This means that legally no physical invoice needs to be kept, considering that its digital version is. That being, if you receive the digital invoice by email, you can destroy the physical copy. 

We advise you to double check if all physical invoices have also been received by email, in order to avoid loosing any of them. If you find that any of the virtual invoices are missing, please make sure to scan the physical invoice and store it before destroying it.  

Also, before destroying any physical copies, check with the tax and billing teams if there are any internal requirements.

Hi[~accountid:63a583d78a07cbd184a96e54] Photos of dishes are protected by copyright. Your described situation where “many providers contacted by us claim they have no pictures / saying we should use their pictures available on other platforms such as Wolt” indicates that the providers do not own rights to the photos, but the rights holder is Wolt. 

Competitors like Wolt monitor us closely. We have received take-down notices from Wolt in the past. We had received photos from a restaurant, but copyright to the photos belonged to Wolt and we needed to remove the photos. So, we have already experienced that providers do not know or care about copyright. As Debora explained, Bolt will be responsible for the infringement, not the provider. 

If we repeatedly infringe Wolt’s rights, their patience might end and they may request us to pay damages. The amount could be a 4-5 figure sum per photo. We could better use that money to make photos of our own.

It is possible that rights to the photos belong to providers. In that case we can use the photos with their consent. However, again it would be very difficult to verify whether they actually own the rights. We can ask them specific questions, like: 1. who made the photos? 2. did you paid for making the photos? and 3. did you sign an agreement with the photographer?, and ask them to sign a confirmation/indemnification letter (so that they bear all costs if we receive an infringement claim from Wolt or any other third person).

In the end, we need to rely on their confirmation, and understand the risk that most partners usually don’t know who owns the copyright. If the provider’s confirmation proves wrong and Wolt requests damages from us, Bolt needs to pay. We cannot direct the claim to the partner, but can only request compensation from the provider. If the provider does not have money, we will not get any compensation. 

Ultimately “increasing number of pictures of dishes on our platforms” needs a business decision whether to hire a photographer (like Wolt has done) or take photos from third parties and risk with the infringement actions and payment of damages.

[~accountid:5de0e6d708d48c0d13acbb53] - you guys made a great list of various “expectations” or “thoughts” regarding the topic. Maybe few overarching comments.

*Goal*: proposing to re-purpose it from “accounting level” controls into - just data quality controls. There is such concept of “materiality” - depending on the purpose and use case - same thing can be either material and important or not. When we talk about Finance / Commerce as one of the users of DAP - we are just a bit more often a bit more demanding as we are facing external compliance of Bolt and ensuring that we can continue operating business. But at the end of the day - IMO - until we know (informed) how much something is “broken” “as of now” - we can’t really judge is it material only for finance or for finance and growth or just for rides or … you name whom. We can’t use “hope” based approach IMO even in cases when data is used only monthly.

When we know that right now this thing is out of sync for this much - only based on this we can decide that we must fix ASAP or wait until “tomorrow”.  So having control in place is a no brainer starting point IMO. And later actioning strategy might be different.



*Control strategies*: in the deck you describe one of them. But different tables might have different ones applied. Somewhere count, somewhere count by dimension(s), somewhere amounts (by period or period + dimensions) or sometimes it is full-to-full (like master data tables). Whatever we will do - I’m sure we will employ different ones for different cases depending on the downstream risks / dependencies on this data. 



*Escalations*: I would propose to consider “eventual consistency” principle in this topic as well. We know that we have async dynamic processes on source <> sync <> destination. It should be fine. But often there are data stabilization models. like if you know that your “yesterday” data changes over next 3 days and you can have materiality levels as well - you will say - escalate only IF this does not get to matching on day 3 for 100% or on day 1 for 99%. so you will have a dynamic case by case approach (nb! but there will be “few” patterns overall)



*Lifecycle*: 

we are currently focusing on “detecting” stuff. But maybe we would also need to consider more broader e2e scope like:

* prevent
* get indirect suspects that it might be higher risk
* detect if something happened (including re-run for last … day-month-year-two years… )
* action (re-sync or ..) - includes anything from fixing down to post mortem if needed
* evidence control executions (a) for ourselves as we must be on top of actual  control efficiency at any point in time (b) external audits  / due diligence (c) next step
*  analyze dynamics of pipelines, non standard situations and correlations of various data points. 



*Project duration*:. Maybe I would not be scared and say “it will take year”. I feel that we can propose extendable engine and people around can contribute. into it. And then iterate fast on this engine capabilities as they highly likely be very generic still.

{{full_eta_exact_s}}: This is the exact eta from driver current location to rider pickup point. If driver is b2b, then it includes the current trip duration to destination as well.
{{eta_shown_s}}: As far as I understand, this is rounded off {{full_eta_exact_s}} to closest minute or ceiling of full minute. We receive this from geo.
{{b2b_dropoff_eta_exact_s}}: This is the exact eta for b2b driver's current trip destination to rider pickup point.
{{b2b_dropoff_eta_s}}: As far as I understand, this is rounded off {{b2b_dropoff_eta_exact_s}} to closest minute or ceiling of full minute. We receive this from geo.

All these fields are in {{seconds}}.

For FOO requests, we are sending {{eta_shown_s}} in {{eta}} field and {{b2b_dropoff_eta_s}} in {{b2b_dropoff_duration}} field.

* A Bolt, enquanto plataforma eletrónica, deve atestar o cumprimento dos requisitos legais e regulamentares aplicáveis aos veículos durante todo o período no qual os mesmos se encontram registados na nossa plataforma, sendo obrigação legal o bloqueio dos veículos que se encontram em incumprimento de tais requisitos.

* Assim, recomendamos que os documentos atualizados dos veículos sejam atempadamente enviados de forma a evitar tais situações.

FYI - I see that they are referring to _Local Government (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 1976,  Sections 55/56_

Section 56 states: 

*Operators of private hire vehicles.* 

(1)For the purposes of this Part of this Act every contract for the hire of a private hire vehicle licensed under this Part of this Act shall be deemed to be made with the operator who accepted the booking for that vehicle whether or not he himself provided the vehicle. 

(2)Every person to whom a licence in force under section 55 of this Act has been granted by a district council shall keep a record in such form as the council may, by condition attached to the grant of the licence, prescribe and shall enter therein, before the commencement of each journey, such particulars of every booking of a private hire vehicle invited or accepted by him, whether by accepting the same from the hirer or by undertaking it at the request of another operator, as the district council may by condition prescribe and s*hall produce such record on request to any authorised officer of the council or to any constable for inspection.* 

(3)Every person to whom a licence in force under section 55 of this Act has been granted by a district council shall keep such records as *the council may, by conditions attached to the grant of the licence, prescribe of the particulars of any private hire vehicle operated by him and shall produce the same on request to any authorised officer of the council or to any constable for inspection.* 

(4)A person to whom a licence in force under section 55 of this Act has been granted by a district council shall produce the licence on request to any authorised officer of the council or any constable for inspection. 

(5)If any person without reasonable excuse contravenes the provisions of this section, he shall be guilty of an offence.

I would like to add some comments about testing. As you may know, we have two DB environments – Live and Prelive. We have a cronjob that syncs the Live data to Prelive environment every night at a specific time. If these changes are not applied to Live as well, they get wiped out by the next nightly sync. Have you considered testing the new index on Prelive environment first? You will be able to clearly see the difference in disk space or other resources.

When it comes to non-metadata changes (like adding new indexes), we utilize [gh-ost tool|https://github.com/github/gh-ost] for making alterations. It creates a new table on MySQL instances, applies alters to it, and then copies the data from the original table. Backend requests go to the old table until the new table is ready. It has a throttle mechanism that pauses data copying sometimes to prevent gh-ost from taking resources needed for production workload, so it does not affect backend workload.
As I can see, there is no significant load on a cluster where {{taxify_delivery_invoicing}} schema is located; so I don’t expect any problems during the alteration process.

After analysing your question we have concluded the following:

Clause 12.2. L) explicitly forbids passengers from engaging in behaviours that can be classified as threats to anyone. 
* Clause 12.3 establishes that the consequence for anyone involved in such behaviours can be either “_immediate, temporary or permanent withdrawal of the Passenger's right to use the Bolt Service_” or “_immediate, temporary or permanent removal of any User Content_;”. 
* This means that their +rider account can be targeted for sanctions for violation of the T&C+. 
* Regarding their driver accounts, the T&C for passengers also establish, in clause 12.4, the following: “_The actions described in clause 12.3 are not limited and Bolt may take any other action it reasonably considers appropriate._”
* This statement, plus the one on clause 2.4.5. of the T&C for TVDE operators (that states “_You will not use the Software for illegal or unauthorized purposes that may impair the proper functioning of the Software;_) +leave room for action against their driver accounts+. 



Conclusion, both T&C leave room for action against both the driver accounts and passenger accounts. Nonetheless, please considers that deciding to act against the drivers account creates a reclassification risk. Therefore, you must undergo an analysis on whether a security blockage should be applied on such cases, given this risk.

Hey team,

{quote}# Can you let me know how commission is charged to a driver in a principal market - where cash is enabled?{quote}

Commission is calculated as usual. % or a fixed sum over ride price. What principal market translates to in terms of invoicing is: Bolt buys the ride from the driver and sells it with a higher price to the rider (simply adding mark-up). Monthly aggregated invoice for drivers in principal model is simply the sum of App payments - booking fee - commission + bonuses (if any).

{quote}* If a driver gets into negative balance what happens - how do we recoup the commission?
** Usual debt collection process. We first send them a message at a previously set threshold (let’s say A) that we will block their cash rides when their negative balance hits B. When the balance hits B, we block their cash rides until they make a payment which would bring their balance to C. Values A,B,C can be set by Billing.
* How do cash payments impact pricing tests where there is dynamic commission?
** I am not sure about that. Sounds more like a question to pricing team.
* What happens if a driver only completes cash trips, how do they eventually pay commission?
** Debt collection. Their balance would be negative, so we would ask them to pay their negative balance{quote}



{quote}2.What internal settings need to be changed to turn on cash payments in the UK? Do we need to update the fee calculator?{quote}

We would need to set the cashblocking limits I’ve mentioned above (values A,B,C) calculated by Billing Analytics (cc: [~accountid:61c450c9e67ea2006b2caf9e]), which would eventually autoatically block/unblock cash rides for drivers. Other than that, the process is owned by Local Operations so I am not sure what is required to enable it in the first place. [~accountid:61c450c9e67ea2006b2caf9e] would you have any input?

We want to ensure that Bolt platform continues to uphold the highest privacy standards for our customers. Recently, we have received inquiries from our customers about the use of *audio recording measures* by ${you/name the driver or courier}.

We would like to express our concern regarding this practice when there is a lack of necessary steps taken to ensure compliance with the respective privacy law. 

We aim to provide you with some important information:

You are considered independent data controllers under privacy regulations. This means that you are responsible for ensuring that your use of *audio recording measures* aligns with local and EU laws, particularly with regard to privacy and data protection.

If you use *audio recording measures*, we recommend that you ensure that you have the *audio recording* sign and enhance it by providing key details such as the purpose of the *audio recording*, the controller's name, the data retention period, and information on where customers can access a comprehensive *audio recording* privacy notice. Kindly ensure that you inform customers about the processing of their personal data and *audio* *recordings*.

Hi Hendrik!

I have discussed this with a Safety Incident Manager and Risk Team and these are the conclusions we have reached.

This report falls under [Driver Inappropriate Behaviour|https://beehive.bolt.eu/main/kb/articles/internal/39795]. Let me try to explain. “Good time” does not necessarily mean anything sexual related (although it’s plausible this is what the driver meant). It could be anything from having a chat in the car, little flirtation, asking the rider out for a coffee or actually offering/asking for sexual relations. Since *we don´t know for sure*  what the driver meant and *we cannot assume* either then we have to go with inappropriate behaviour.

Whatever the driver actually meant - it made the rider uncomfortable and therefore it became a safety issue. Since we can’t prove this happened and we can’t assume anything then it’s Minor and the driver should be educated to avoid such comments or warned (depending on his history).

[Driver Use Of Any Sexual Talk|https://beehive.bolt.eu/main/kb/articles/internal/39795] is, however, much more serious, because the driver is actually talking about sexual topics (in a general context ) or talking about sexual matters in direct relation to himself or the rider (e.g. How often does the rider have sex? What does the driver prefer in the bedroom etc. - sorry for specific examples, but they help to understand EC better)

So, in conclusion - Driver Inappropriate Behaviour is much broader an EC as Driver Use of Any Sexual Talk. And this example falls under the first category. Hope this makes sense!

[~accountid:6038f479f6ccc000705e716a], I would consider each point separately:

# This is a unilateral NDA - I assume that we will not share any confidential information about Bolt Business or it’s scope will be very limited, so I don’t see great legal risk here.
# Definition of confidential information is not well defined - it would be easier for the counterparty to say that we breached our confidentiality obligations and this is not according to the industry standard as there are well known exceptions that are normally present in the definition of confidential information (for example, information that is publicly available), but at the same time, it is generally hard to prove breach of confidential obligations. Therefore, the legal risk is balanced, although, we need to be cautious.
# Sharing information amongst group companies - the risk is low that this will be pursued by them.
# Monetary penalty - penalty is not that big and it has some caveats (they will first ask to eliminate breach and ask to pay penalty if irreversible damage was caused as a result of the breach), so it is generally ok.
# No specified term - Bolt will always be under obligation to keep confidential information safe - so they can bring claim at any point of time if we breach our obligations - we just need to make sure that we treat their information with caution.

So from the legal point of view there are no hard blockers although terms are not favourable and have certain risks, mainly monetary (penalty + compensation for damages caused by our breach).

Clause 8.16.2 states that _“at the termination of this Agreement [the Tenant] shall reinstate the Premises to the same good order and condition in which it was as at the commencement date, fair wear and tear excepted.”._ 

Furthermore, there is not general legal principle that states a premises that has been leased out commercially requires the tenant to detail clean upon the termination of the lease.

In the circumstances, I suggest that you quote this clause to the landlord and state that you will not sign the exit inspection form until reference to detail cleaning and white box is removed as it it not required.

Chapter 38 § 2 of the Code of Judicial Procedure,
Possesses any written document, which can be assumed to be of importance as evidence, he is obliged to produce it; however, such obligation does not fall on the suspect in criminal cases or the person who is in such a relationship with him, as referred to in ch. 36. Section 3.

Neither the party nor his close relatives, as has just been said, is obliged to provide written notice between the party and anyone close to him or between such close relatives. Executive or other, as referred to in ch. 36 Section 5, may not present a written document, if its content can be assumed to be such that he may not be heard as a witness to it; if the document is held by a party, in whose favor the duty of confidentiality applies, he is not obliged to present the document. The statute in ch. 36 Section 6 on the witness's right to refuse to testify has a corresponding application in the case of the holder of a written document, if its content is such as is referred to in the aforementioned law room.

The obligation to present a written document does not apply to a memorial note or other such record, which is intended exclusively for personal use, unless there is a special reason for it to be presented.

According to practice, written documents also mean electronically stored information. Supreme Court decisions: NJA 1981 p 791, NJA 1992 p 307, NJA 2015 p 631 and 2020 p 373.

The contract was sent out for signature. By know, counterparty should have received an email with a spotdraft notification/invitation to sign.

*Implications from tracking user’s impressions for certain items (such as sexual wellbeing items (condoms, lubricants), health-related products (pregnant test, COVID test, diabetes test, any other items related to a specific disease,* {color:#bf2600}*excluding* {color}*thermometer, tonometers, food supplements, sport-related items or other medical items used by the wider public (bandages, plasters, cold pills)*



To assess the risks from the project, we have to start from whether the data is considered special category of data that are prohibited from any processing, unless some conditions are met (one of them is an explicit consent of the user)

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Are sexual wellbeing items and health-related products special category of data?*
{panel}

The European Law (GDPR) states that any data revealing sex life, sexual orientation or health of an individual is a special category of data. There are no clear criteria to understand the threshold for “_revealing_”. 
[According to CJEU case,|https://curia.europa.eu/juris/document/document.jsf;jsessionid=E7212ECF38E8EAB7DBC2AB443FD6B4C1?text=&docid=263721&pageIndex=0&doclang=EN&mode=lst&dir=&occ=first&part=1&cid=2255189] to be recognised special category of data _“it should be determined whether_ *_data that are capable of revealing the sexual orientation_* _of a natural person_ *_by means of an intellectual operation involving comparison or deduction_* _fall within the special categories of personal data, for the purpose of Article 8(1) of Directive 95/46 and Article 9(1) of the GDPR”._ Literally saying, *there is no criteria of the controller’s purpose* *of the processing activity* *or intention to reveal this information* rather than the mere fact of this data being capable to reveal the sexual orientation, life or health of an individual even in theory. The level of inference is not specified in the case, eg it’s not clear whether a small piece of data can provide a picture about the sex life or sexual orientation of the person.

[Another case analysed by Norwegian DPA|https://edpb.europa.eu/news/national-news/2021/norwegian-dpa-imposes-fine-against-grindr-llc_en] advises that the name of an individual and the mere fact that the individual is a part of the app created for sexual minorities is the special category of data. This case also implicitly states that there is no criteria of the controller’s purpose rather than the capability to deduct the info related to sex life or sexual orientation of the individual from this data.

At the same time, neither WP Article 29, nor EDPB, nor Recitals of the GDPR states any criteria for recognising data as _“revealing”._

On the other side, ICO states that _“Special category data includes personal data_ *_revealing or concerning_* _the above types of data. Therefore, if you have inferred or guessed details about someone which fall into one of the above categories, this data may count as special category data._ *_It depends on how certain that inference is, and whether you are deliberately drawing that inference”._* Meaning that the inference and the controller’s purpose can be vital. However, Bolt Market does not operate in the UK, so the ICO’s opinion is not decisive.

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Privacy Legal Team’s position on sexual wellbeing items and health-related products as a special category of data*
{panel}

While the CJEU decision and NO DPA opinion do not specify anything in relation to the certainty of such an inference, eg whether information should provide a whole picture about the individual’s sex life or even be a small part that could contribute to the understanding of the individual’s sex life. 

Bolt processes user’s order history that can include sexual wellbeing items for packing the order and delivering the order to the user. Following the CJEU decision and NO DPA case, Privacy Legal Team does not believe that the mere fact of understanding how frequently the user buys sexual wellbeing items can reveal (or is capable of revealing) sex life of an individual rather than to contribute to the bigger analysis. As Bolt does not collect or cross-check this data with any other data of the individual that can contribute to the analysis of the sex life of the user, Privacy Legal Team sees that this data is not special category of data as it is not capable to reveal the sex life of an individual. 

In terms of impression tracking, where Bolt’s purpose is to track user’s interaction with the app for the sole purpose of analysing the Bolt Market items performance, poor performing brands and UI experience of the user, the mere fact of knowing how much time the user spent on the page with sexual wellbeing items and whether the user clicked on these items and put them into the basket, does not seem to reveal the information about the user’s sex life.

At the same time, Privacy Legal Team recognises that these items are sensitive for the users and appropriate technical and organisational measures should be taken into account for their protection  (as for financial data that are considered more sensitive, but not special). 

*Based on the CJEU decision and analysis above, the Privacy Legal Team would NOT classify sexual well-being items and other health-related products* intended for tracking in the Menu Item Impression Tracking system *as special categories of data. However, the Privacy Legal Team acknowledges their sensitive nature.* 

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Any negative impact on the Bolt Market users from Menu Item Impression Tracking project*
{panel}

# *Intrusion into Privacy and User’s Trust:* Users can find the tracking of their app interactions (especially sexual wellbeing items and other health-related products) as intrusive or unnecessary. This may result in users being less inclined to engage with the app or share their data in the future. In addition, users may be concerned about the extent of data collection and how it is being used.
# *Data Security and Data Misuse:* There is *always* a risk of data breaches and unauthorized access to the information collected during user interactions with the app. This could lead to the exposure of sensitive user data to malicious actors who can misuse or repurpose this data, leading to potential privacy violations or discrimination of users

*At the same time, there are no direct negative consequences to the users such as blocking, banning users from Bolt’s platforms, targeting users with the specific content, using this data for marketing, behaviour advertisement or profiling, or sharing this data with any third party.*

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*If Privacy Legal Team takes the stand that sexual wellbeing items and health-related products could be recognised as a special category of data, is the explicit consent viable solution for Bolt?*
{panel}

There are some business implications for the consent we need to consider:
*Rules for consent:* We should have a new checkbox asking for user's consent to this and *have a detailed explanation on why we need this*, right to decline this, and right to revoke the consent in the app easily and quickly.
*Ethics:* A reasonable person could be negatively impressed by this consent for tracking impressions on this sensitive category and we would be buried with complaints on why we need this and how it correlates with the goal of Bolt Market. Users can raise this on social media as well.
*Regulator's attention:* Regulator’s can approach us if someone reports or they see a wave on social media. They will dive deeper in the process of impression tracking and unfold all our gaps with the deletion process and retention periods that we do not have right now. They would ask which measures we put in place to make it anonymous (unlink the user from these impressions). 
*Consent is not a panacea* and we should still think of unlinking this data or other technical or organisational controls.
*Brand's attention:* implementing consent and the attention to us due to this consent can raise brands' concerns and it can affect their presence on a platform.

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Privacy Legal Team recommendation*
{panel}

As the criteria for recognising the data as special category of data is not defined in the GDPR, there is a risk the the data protection authority would see the data used for this project as special category of data, while the Privacy Legal Team analysis states otherwise.
We recommend considering to:

* *do not track sensitive data:* implement the process where certain items will be marked as “sensitive” and will not be tracked; or
* *anonymise (not possible at all to link the data with the user) or de-identify data (implement measures that reduce the risk of data being link to the user):* if the team wants to proceed with the tracking, the team should come up with the way to unlink the impressions for sensitive categories from the user profile and ID right after the collection and have a separate flow for analysing this anonymised data.

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Consequences if the data is recognised as a special category of data by the data protection authority*
{panel}

In this case, it could be recognised that Bolt did not have a legal basis to process this data (as conditions under Art 9 of the GDPR for special data processing are not met). The regulator is in power to:

# issue a warning and ask to adjust the project; 
# ask for the user’s consent; and
# temporarily or permanently stop the processing and delete the data collected before.

Project Overview Document provided by Ops {color:#4c9aff}({color}[{color:#4c9aff}+here+{color}|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1XokFqkQfn5kWx0TRWB55EhHaM-N71rzC3fluxEmQOcw/edit#heading=h.olo5ld8vrdv1]{color:#4c9aff}+)+{color}

17 January 2024 review of the project 

+*REVIEW OF PROJECT KODAK*+ 

# {color:#ff991f}*CCTV PARTNERSHIP* {color}

Bolt will be acting as an introducer, introducing the driver to the partner (who offers the CCTV). Bolt will be promoting this benefit to the drivers. 

Intention is for there to be an agreement between Bolt and the Partner, then the Partner will have a separate agreement in place with the Driver. - do you have any draft versions of what the agreement between the partner and Bolt will look like? Will Bolt have sight of the agreement between the partner and the driver, whilst Bolt is not a party to this agreement, it may be helpful to have sight of how this may look. 

You mention that the partner will be providing Bolt with the details on how many vehicles have had CCTV installed and uninstalled. I am assuming that the driver must be providing consent for this information to be shared. 

The privacy team would need to conduct a review on this project and provide comments on the data sharing aspects and if there are any red flags in regards to this. 

+*WHAT HAPPENS IF A SAFETY INCIDENT OCCURS*+ 

You mention that drivers (who will be the data processors) will have the option to provide Bolt with the footage but will not be required to do so. If the driver does not consent the incident will be investigated in the usual way. 

+*WHAT ARE THE BENEFITS TO THE PARTNER COMPANY*+

The partner will  benefit from being alerted if there is an incident having a chance to make offers to the driver on how to manage it. The partner will try to promote other strands of their business to the driver for example: representing the driver for the accident on a “no win no fee basis”, putting the driver in contact with courtesy car companies etc. 

How much does it cost for a driver to get this CCTV installed? 

+*WHAT IS THE INCENTIVE FOR THE DRIVER*+ 

For the driver the incentive is that having CCTV installed in their vehicle can act as a deterrent for any incidents to occur on the journey. It will also help the driver mitigate against any claims made by a passenger. In addition, insurance companies may offer cheaper insurance to drivers on the basis that they have CCTV installed in their vehicle. 

+*DOES THIS HAVE AN EFFECT ON BOTH THE AGENCY AND PRINCIPLE MODEL*+ 

From my understanding Bolt is no longer changing the business model to an agency model, therefore this question is not applicable. 

+*REVIEW OF EXTERNAL ADVICE BOLT HAS RECEIVED TO DATE REGARDING RECLASSIFICATION*+ 

Bolt is advised by Lewis Silkin to avoid any features which would indicate that the driver is integrated into Bolt. See snapshot of advice below: 

h4. “Lewis Silkin advice note - July 2022

(iii) Avoid other features that are indicative of integration: for example, you have referred to access to leased and/or branded vehicles and insurance perks via a funding allowance as a benefit of worker status, but this does not mean you need to compel drivers to use a particular vehicle while working for Bolt, or to take up your insurance offering rather than spending the money elsewhere, and you could make this clear”. 

+*WHAT HAPPENS IF THE DRIVER LEAVES BOLT?*+ 

If the driver stops working for Bolt how will this work? Do the drivers have to have the CCTV uninstalled by the partner or does the driver get to carry on using the CCTV equipment? I raise this question as it is the driver who will be bearing the cost of installing the CCTV. 

+*ARE THERE ANY RECLASSIFICATION RISKS*+ 

In the Uber case, it was determined that drivers should be classified as workers due to various factors, one of which was the significant control exerted by Uber. This control was examined through five key dimensions:

* Financial control
* Contractual control
* Acceptance of riders control
* Scope of services control
* Information control

Drivers are given a choice on whether or not they want to contact the partner provider and install the CCTV in their vehicles as opposed to the drivers being forced to have this in their vehicle. Given that Bolt is not imposing this as a requirement for drivers to use the Bolt platform, there are no major red flags here as there is no ‘contractual control’ being exerted onto the driver.  Bolt is acting as an introducer only (promoting the partner to the driver)*.* 

I would need to review the agreement between Bolt and the CCTV Partner to provide a more deeper analysis. 

Whilst Bolt is not a party to the contract between the driver and the Partner CCTV company, how will it work in terms of the CCTV Partner company providing you statistics on how many drivers have had this installed/uninstalled? # CCTV SUBSIDY

Purpose: is to improved safety for both driver and passenger

I have two concerns with this initiative:

+*Concern 1*+ 

Generally, Bolt should avoid offering drivers any incentives (subsidising CCTV payments for drivers) that are indicative of integration into Bolt. The reason is, if Bolt provides subsidised payments for drivers this may raise questions about the true working relationship between drivers and Bolt. Independent contractors should maintain autonomy and control over their work, by Bolt paying for drivers CCTV it may be seen as Bolt providing the driver with the resources to work which may create a perception that the contractor is more like an employee, potentially jeopardising the contractor's status as an independent worker. In addition, Subsidising payments for drivers may create an expectation that Bolt is providing additional benefits (which is traditionally associated with employees) such as health, again blurring the lines between independent contractor and employee relationships.

+*Concern 2*+ 

[Option A] Selected drivers are enrolled in a campaign which will be visible in their app

[Option B] Alternatively, selected drivers are simply contacted by email and/or in-app message with the details of the offer

You mention that only qualified drivers will be eligible for either option A or option B. Bolt selects drivers who are eligible for the campaign, targeting existing *_top drivers_*. Top drivers will be identified based on:

* Number of finished orders within the past 3 months - this will ensure that Bolt's take from these drivers’ activity is already higher than the price for the cameras.
* Activity score (i.e. acceptance X completion rate: calculated based on the last 80 orders that a driver receives within their selected radius. The activity score increases when the driver accepts and completes a trip and decreases when orders are rejected, cancelled, or not responded to).
* Metrics will be city specific (a top driver in London for example would not be considered as a top driver in Birmingham) and monitored monthly.
* Quarterly review will be done to assess the requirements to make sure they are still relevant on a city by city basis.

* The offer will be limited to drivers who are also the vehicle owners (i.e. not renting the vehicle from a rental company / fleet).

By Bolt only allowing top drivers to be included in the campaign as opposed to this being offered to all drivers, this may be construed as Bolt excluding drivers who do not fall within the ‘top drivers’ category. Essentially, if a driver does not complete X amount of trips or maintain an acceptable activity score then the driver would not be considered to meet the threshold of ‘top driver’. This could slip into the realms of contractual control and acceptance of riders control blurring the lines between independent contractor and employee relationships.

Hi Antoni,

After analysing your question we have concluded the following:

* The T&C for passengers (available here: [https://bolt.eu/en-pt/legal/tnc-passengers/?category=rides|https://bolt.eu/en-pt/legal/tnc-passengers/?category=rides|smart-link] ) establish rules of conduct. Clause 12.2. L) explicitly forbids passengers from engaging in behaviours that can be classified as threats to anyone.
* Clause 12.3 establishes that the consequence for anyone involved in such behaviours can be either “_immediate, temporary or permanent withdrawal of the Passenger's right to use the Bolt Service_” or “_immediate, temporary or permanent removal of any User Content_;”.
* This means that their +rider account can be targeted for sanctions for violation of the T&C+.
* Regarding their driver accounts, the T&C for passengers also establish, in clause 12.4, the following: “_The actions described in clause 12.3 are not limited and Bolt may take any other action it reasonably considers appropriate._”
* This statement, plus the one on clause 2.4.5. of the T&C for TVDE operators (that states “_You will not use the Software for illegal or unauthorized purposes that may impair the proper functioning of the Software;_) +leave room for action against their driver accounts+.



In conclusion, both T&Cs leave room for action against both the driver and passenger accounts of the same individual.

Nonetheless, please consider that acting against the driver’s account through suspension or permanent account blocking creates a reclassification risk and Portugal is currently one of the markets with the highest reclassification risk. Additionally, in Portugal it has been decided to only block driver accounts in 3 scenarios: compliance, safety and fraud. Therefore, you must undergo an analysis in case the decision is to take action through suspension or permanent account blocking on whether a) this is an event under safety and whether b) it should be applied on such cases given the high reclassification risk.

Please let me know if you have any other questions. Thank you.

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on 01 February 2024.

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software.Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail,  we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.

Yours sincerely,

Bolt

Dear Fouad



*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 

 

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *25th November 2023.*

 

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software.Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail,  we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

 

We are sharing copies of the personal data we hold about *you* to which you are entitled. This includes:

* *ID documentation*
* *Driver profile, registration, and checks information*
* *Block data*
* *Change log registration*
* *Driver device history and log in sessions*
* *Driver ride history*
* *Confirmation rate*
* *Driver dispatch preferences*
* *Driver status logs*
* *Selected car history*
* *Time driver spent in status*
* *Average rating*
* *Driver rating comments*
* *Payouts*

 

Please be advised that you have access to all your financial information via Driver Portal available at[ Sign Up as a Bolt Driver | Bolt|https://partners.bolt.eu/login?isPasswordReset=true&shortlink=lvew0z3s&c=Global] by navigating through the following areas:

· *Invoices, pay statements, balance reports* 

 

o   Invoices:

§ Invoices issued to riders from you as a driver available at[ Sign Up as a Bolt Driver | Bolt|https://partners.bolt.eu/rider-invoices]

§ Invoices issued to you as a driver by Bolt[ Sign Up as a Bolt Driver | Bolt|https://partners.bolt.eu/invoices]

·  Pay statements can be accessed via Payouts available at[ |https://partners.bolt.eu/payout][Sign Up as a Bolt Driver | Bolt|https://partners.bolt.eu/payout]

·  Balance reports available at[Sign Up as a Bolt Driver | Bolt|https://partners.bolt.eu/balance-reports]

 

For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our Privacy Policy at [https://bolt.eu/fr-fr/privacy/privacy-for-drivers/?category=rides|https://bolt.eu/fr-fr/privacy/privacy-for-drivers/?category=rides|smart-link] , which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.

 

*Your rights* 

 

In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data,restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 

 

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.

 

Yours sincerely,

Bolt

In rides and micromobility core datasets we have defined semantic models. The very purpose of semantic models is to provide this kind of information. However, it’s probably not in the format you’d expect for traditional use cases 🙂 

I did want to point out that with metrics you can run a query like this

{noformat}mf list dimensions --metrics metric1,metric2{noformat}

and it will return a list of common dimensions for the two metrics. Because the use case for metrics is different, it won’t tell you the join keys, but it will tell you on which grains you could calculate these two measures together.

Hey [~accountid:712020:46da73ea-bcbb-4b69-8e3e-ac27402d61bc] here are some thoughts:

* Indeed the tvde law states a general prohibition of branding in TVDE vehicles in article 12(8): “ É proibida a colocação ou exibição de publicidade no interior ou exterior do veículo que efetue TVDE.”

* What is meant by publicity is not defined in the TVDE or taxi legislation. 
* However, the Publicity Code in Portugal defines it as “any form of communication made by… private entities, in the context of a commercial… or liberal activity, with the direct or *indirect* aim of:
a) Promoting, with a view to their commercialisation or sale, any goods or services;
b) *Promoting* ideas, principles, initiatives or *institutions*.”
* It appears the proposal above is likely to be regarded as publicity since it would be promoting indirectly Bolt and consequently be under the general prohibition.
* The risk is that Bolt and TVDE operators could be facing possible fines in the amount between 5k to 15k.

Hi Bartosz, 

Seems that needed information hasn’t been shared with you, as a manager, and with the employee mentioned by your People Partner, as to what steps are taken with equity compensation when employee switches over from their employment contract to B2B contract.

As a rule, Bolt grants equity compensation only to its employees and all option holders in Carta have their relationship status listed as an employee. When employee is exiting the company then their grants are terminated as per [usual process|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/BILP/pages/3748954176/Bolt+s+Option+Program#When-leaving-Bolt]. This process is also followed even when employee is switching over to B2B contract, as their employment relationship is coming to an end.
All unvested units from employment relationship grant(s) are moved over to new grant(s), and custom vesting schedule is added to the grants to make sure that these vest as they would have if employment relationship would have remained in place. Relationship status for these grants will be listed as consultant. 

Such approach is needed to reduce the risk of declassification and also have clear separation between “employee” and “consultant” grants for tax and legal purposes.

Let me know if any questions.

Kind regards

Hi [~accountid:712020:5c3f18cd-53ab-40ca-9fae-fb38035ab6d8], 

The referenced section in the Criminal Procedural Code (38:2) states the duty to disclose, also known as the obligation to share documents or information. This is a fundamental principle within the legal system that requires parties in a lawsuit to share relevant documents and information with each other and with the court. For this duty to apply, certain requirements must be met:

# *Legal Proceedings*: The duty typically applies in the context of ongoing litigation or a legal proceeding.
# *Relevance*: The information or documents being requested must be relevant to the current legal process. This means they must have some significance to the dispute or to assessing the case.
# *Request*: Usually, one party must request the relevant documents or information from the other party. This can be done through formal requests or within the framework of legal procedures such as discovery.
# *Obligation to Respond*: If a request for disclosure is justified, the other party has an obligation to respond to the request properly and within a reasonable time.
# *Court Approval*: In some cases, the court may be involved in overseeing the disclosure process and may require parties to share certain information or documents.

In summary, the duty to disclose must be relevant to the *ongoing legal process* and comply with procedural rules and procedures to be applicable.

As we have received a request from the police in this case I would not deem that there are any ongoing legal proceedings, rather it seems to still be in the investigation stage, and therefore the referenced sections would not be applicable.

[Addison Lee Settlement|https://www.leighday.co.uk/news/news/2024-news/settlement-reached-for-addison-lee-drivers-in-workers-rights-claim/]:

* In the last few days Leigh Day has reached a settlement with Addison Lee for three drivers.
* The settlement comes after a decision in by the Employment Tribunal in 2017 that Addison Lee drivers are workers. This judgment was upheld by the Employment Appeal Tribunal (EAT) in 2018 and Court of Appeal in 2021.
* Specific sums of the settlement paid to these 3 Driver are not public, press reporting suggests wider impact will be in the tens of millions.
* While the claim was originally brought by these three drivers, over 600 drivers are now represented by Leigh Day. Addison Lee continues to argue that the 2017 judgment does not apply to the other claimants who had subsequently brought claims.
* A hearing is due to take place in October and November 2024 to determine whether the rest of the claimants are workers and entitled to workers’ rights.
* The Leigh Day claims page for Addison Lee now says this – “[Addison Lee drivers who join the claim will be entitled to around £10,000 in compensation|https://www.leighday.co.uk/our-services/group-claims/addison-lee-driver-claim/]”.
* LS have commented that there is no way LD could say this based on actual losses given it would vary between Drivers (hours worked, holiday accrued, fees paid), therefore they believe that this has been a set commercial amount per Driver based on the information available publicly.
* Therefore, their Settlement above of £10K per Driver may be similar to what Bolt's first Stage 1 Option A offer has been - except this was £300 per Driver - with £10K.

Thanks for getting back. In KE we do not have a cash test for couriers. As IH, on escalation, we check the courier’s debt, and if it’s within the cash-enabling threshold(KES 1,800) we activate the cash orders. More to note is that the KES 1800 cash enabling threshold is different from the cash orders threshold, which is currently KES 4500. If a courier gets their debt above KES 4500, their cash orders are disabled, then they would have to lower the debt to below Ksh 1800 to get their cash orders activated. The reason for the difference between the cash orders threshold and cash enabling threshold is to incentivize couriers to pay their debt and not allow debt to go beyond the threshold

Hi, we unfortunately currently don’t really have the capabilities for such analysis.

If you want to take a look at the logs yourself, these two tables should be helpful:

* {{ng_public.all_presto_clusters_query_event_view}} is a log of Presto queries.
* {{ng_datalake.presto_table_io}} is derived from the raw log data and makes it easier to find which tables were used in which queries.

These should allow you to see at least how often the tables are queried. The logs also contain some information about runtime and if queries ran out of memory, etc., but keep in mind that these metrics also depend on other factors like parallel queries, or cluster configuration.

And important to note: these logs only include Presto queries, there could be other queries from Spark that are using these tables (notably via dbt), and for Spark queries there are no centralized logs.

Sharing query here, results shared on Slack:

{noformat}select 
date_trunc('week', date(b.invoice_date_local)) as week, 
from_agent_id,
b.currency,
br.vat_percentage,
sum(case when br.type = 'service_fee' then sum else 0 end) as service_fee_sum,
sum(case when br.type = 'service_fee' then vat_sum else 0 end) as service_fee_vat_sum,
sum(case when br.type = 'service_fee' then sum_with_vat else 0 end) as service_fee_sum_with_vat,
sum(case when br.type = 'delivery_fee' then sum else 0 end) as delivery_fee_sum,
sum(case when br.type = 'delivery_fee' then vat_sum else 0 end) as delivery_fee_vat_sum,
sum(case when br.type = 'delivery_fee' then sum_with_vat else 0 end) as delivery_fee_sum_with_vat,
sum(b.total_sum_with_vat) as invoices_total
from etl_billing_invoicing_delivery b
left join etl_billing_invoicing_delivery_row br on br.invoice_id = b.id where from_agent_id = 9178 and b.invoice_type = 'delivery_fleet'
and br.type not in ('courier_tip')
group by 1,2,3,4{noformat}

* 30 pln for delays over 1h

Hi [~accountid:712020:dd196f63-fc49-4d36-a37f-98d0ff95f347], thanks for the valuable input and ideas. As Bartosz is on holiday, I’ll provide some assurance and DAP Ingestion team’s vision. I think lots of what you suggested makes a lot of sense :)

DAP’s long-term version is to provide excellent Data Quality control, not only over the MySQL/TiDB replicated raw data, but the overall data (e.g. including the modelled DBT data). As you can imagine, there is a long way to go to achieve it. 

When we focus on the MySQL/TiDB replicated raw data, the pipeline in simple terms replicates data in such a way: {{MySQL/TiDB -> Change Data Capture (Debezium or TiCDC) -> Kafka -> Spark -> Presto/Databricks}}. We already have quite a lot of monitoring and preventions deployed to make sure that we monitor the metrics of each component of the pipeline, quite a few [monitoring are even at the table level|https://monitor.boltint.net/d/nMuC2Cw7z/delta-lake-ingestion?orgId=1&from=now-1h&to=now], some examples of the pipeline monitoring dashboards

* Monitoring the data flow from MySQL/TiDB → Kafka: [https://monitor.boltint.net/d/nMuC2Cw7z/delta-lake-ingestion?orgId=1&from=now-1h&to=now|https://monitor.boltint.net/d/nMuC2Cw7z/delta-lake-ingestion?orgId=1&from=now-1h&to=now]
* Monitoring Kafka: [https://monitor.boltint.net/d/AEaSQ97mz/cdc-overview?orgId=1|https://monitor.boltint.net/d/AEaSQ97mz/cdc-overview?orgId=1]
* Monitoring the data flow from Kafka → Presto/Databricks: [https://monitor.boltint.net/d/nMuC2Cw7z/delta-lake-ingestion?orgId=1&from=now-1h&to=now|https://monitor.boltint.net/d/nMuC2Cw7z/delta-lake-ingestion?orgId=1&from=now-1h&to=now]

As DAP is a central platform team and DAP serves quite many domain teams (I think at least 50 - 100 domain teams), the *most critical and scalable* way for DAP to continue the Data Quality control initiative is to find a way that's self-service friendly (e.g. how domain teams can self-serve the investigation in a simple way) and scalable for the DAP. As the Ingestion team from DAP has only 4 engineers, if the framework is not carefully designed in such a self-service friendly and scalable way, it would be nearly impossible for such a small team to help investigate all domain teams potential Data Quality issues.

I propose that we take an *iterative approach* and first focus on the FinDWH use case before generalising it to a company-wide solution. We’ll learn a lot (e.g. Control strategies and Escalations as you mentioned) from the output and progress of the FinDWH use case. This will serve both DAP and the other domain teams as a groundwork for the further generic solution.

{noformat}with req_output as (
select rf.flow_run_id, 
	rf.check_run_id, 
	rf.requested_field, 
	o.output_field
from ng_public.etl_verification_document_extraction_requested_fields rf
	left join ng_public.etl_verification_document_extraction_output_fields o 
	on o.provider = rf.provider 
	and rf.requested_field = o.output_field 
	and o.check_run_id = rf.check_run_id 
where rf.provider = 'veritas_model_invoker')
, provider_data_mapping as (
    select provider_field_name,
   		extracted_data_field_name
    from ng_public.document_library_provider_data_mapping pdm
    where provider = 'ocr'
    )
, mapping_cleansed as (
    select conf.*, 
    	extracted_data_field_name
    from ng_public.dim_verification_document_extraction_confidence conf
    join provider_data_mapping pdm 
    on conf.field = pdm.provider_field_name
    )
, uuids as (
select id as flow_run_id,
	uuid as flow_run_uuid,
	created as flow_run_created_date,
	concat('https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/identity-trust/verifications/', uuid) as admin_panel_link
	from glue.ng_public.identity_verification_flow_run
	where created_date >= date '2024-01-01'
)
, all_check_runs as (
select a.*,
	case when error_code = 2 then 'INCORRECT_DOC_TYPE' 
		 when error_code in (7, 101) then 'SYSTEM_ERROR'
		 when error_code = 203 then 'EXTRACTED_DATA_FIELD_VALIDATION_FAILED'
		 when error_code = 163 then 'INVALID_PERSONAL_NUMBER'
		 when error_code = 102 then 'MISSING_DATA'
		 when error_code is null then 'NO_ERROR'
		 else 'OTHER_ERROR' end as error_type
	from (
	select a.id as check_run_id,
		a.flow_run_id,
		a.created as check_run_created,
		a.status as check_run_status,
		cast(json_extract(a.result, '$.reason.code') as INTEGER) as error_code,
		uuids.admin_panel_link,
		uuids.flow_run_uuid,
		uuids.flow_run_created_date
	from ng_pii.taxify_identity_verification_check_run a
	join uuids on uuids.flow_run_id = a.flow_run_id
	where a.created > date '2024-01-01'
	and a.provider = 'veritas_model_invoker'
	and a.check_type = 'document_data_extraction_check'
	and a.status <> 'cancelled'
	) a
)
, check_run_with_ocr_output as (
select ro.flow_run_id, 
	ro.check_run_id, 
	ro.requested_field, 
	ro.output_field, 
	mc.confidence, 
	mc.predicted_ocr_group, 
	mc.threshold, 
	case when mc.confidence >= mc.threshold then true else false end as higher_than_threshold, 
	all_check_runs.error_type,
	all_check_runs.error_code,
	mc.document_library_document_country_code as doc_country,
	mc.document_library_document_type as doc_type,
	'check_run_with_ocr_output' as which_table,
	all_check_runs.flow_run_created_date,
	all_check_runs.check_run_created,
	all_check_runs.flow_run_uuid,
	all_check_runs.admin_panel_link
from req_output ro
	join all_check_runs on all_check_runs.flow_run_id = ro.flow_run_id
		and all_check_runs.check_run_id = ro.check_run_id
	left join mapping_cleansed mc on mc.flow_run_id = ro.flow_run_id 
		and ro.requested_field = mc.extracted_data_field_name
)
, docs_country_types as (
select flow_run_uuid,
	country as doc_country,
	type as doc_type
	from ng_public.identity_verification_document
		where created > date '2024-01-01'
)
, check_run_without_ocr_output as (
select flow_run_id, 
	check_run_id, 
	null as requested_field, 
	null as output_field, 
	null as confidence, 
	null as predicted_ocr_group, 
	null as threshold,
	null as higher_than_threshold,
	error_type,
	error_code,
	doc_country,
	doc_type,
	'check_run_without_ocr_output' as which_table,
	flow_run_created_date,
	check_run_created,
	flow_run_uuid,
	admin_panel_link
from (
	select a.*, 
		b.check_run_id as check_run_with_ocr_output,
		docs_country_types.doc_country,
		docs_country_types.doc_type
	from all_check_runs a
	join docs_country_types on a.flow_run_uuid = docs_country_types.flow_run_uuid
	left join check_run_with_ocr_output b
		on a.flow_run_id = b.flow_run_id
		and a.check_run_id = b.check_run_id
	)
	where check_run_with_ocr_output is null
)
, final as (
select * from check_run_without_ocr_output
union all 
select * from check_run_with_ocr_output
){noformat}

I need you to answer the following questions to prepare T&Cs draft:

# What will be our position regarding undelivered parcels in CZ?
# Will we obtain insurance for parcels?
# What will be the maximum value of parcels that can be transported using Bolt Send?
# Will cash payments be allowed in CZ?

Here is the information related to these questions:

# Undelivered parcels:
## These were options proposed in different markets:
### Baltics: undelivered parcels are brought by drivers to Bolt office/hub or if office/hub is too far away then such parcels are brought to the police station;
### Malta: it is a fleet market and undelivered parcels will be handled by driver/fleet - i.e. driver will bring an undelivered parcel to the fleet's office.
## Problems with these options were:
### Leaving undelivered parcel at Bolt's office - in some markets such practice would require Bolt to have a postal licence. Also, Bolt would be responsible for the parcel whilst in its possession.
### Bringing undelivered parcel to a police station - in some markets police stations would not accept undelivered parcels.
### Letting the fleet to handle undelivered parcel - fleet has to agree to take responsibility for the undelivered parcels and we need to make sure that the customer can easily contact the fleet to reclaim the parcel (with the changes connected to DSA this should not be a problem, but this needs to be double checked).
# Insurance for parcels - it was decided in several markets that securing insurance for parcels is a hassle and the solution was to limit the value of the parcel to 50-150 EUR. This would be the total liability of a driver/fleet for a lost parcel.
# Licence and documents that drivers should have - in some markets drivers/fleets are required to possess a postal licence for transportation of parcels. In some markets, drivers are also required to have transportation documents regarding the parcels - a document that describes what is inside the parcel etc. completed by a customer.
# Cash payments - so far cash payments are not allowed for Bolt Send in the markets that launched or about to launch this category. This is due to the problems associated with asking for additional payments from the customer in case the driver needs to deliver parcel back to the customer if the delivery fails etc.

Please let me know how you would like to proceed and I will prepare the T&Cs.

+*Blocking Matrix*+

The consequential actions suggested by the Global Event Assessment Tool are defined by a Blocking Matrix.

The Blocking Matrix suggests an action that must be taken against the accounts of *reported* users as per the *Risk Type of the Event*, number of *Occurrences* (User’s History) and *Fault Determination* (Who is at fault). Once the information is selected in the Global Event Assessment Tool, a consequential outcome will be suggested.

Additionally, the Tool allows you to take a *Deviant Action* and select a different outcome. When doing so, provide an explanation for your decision.

{color:#ff5630}*TABLES HERE, NO CHANGE*{color}

*NB:* It is not possible to close *Low and Moderate Risk Events* with Cannot Be Confirmed as Fault Determination after the *second* *report* (i.e. from the third Occurrence a Party At Fault must be chosen).

*NB:* It is not possible to close *High and Significant and Risk Events* with Cannot Be Confirmed as Fault Determination after the *first* *report* (i.e. from the second Occurrence a Party At Fault must be chosen).

Hey [~accountid:712020:430ebb39-7e93-404f-8bdb-62aa9c75ce08] [~accountid:712020:0641ea87-e832-482b-8673-ab85e9ad6441] 

# Sharing with you FYI the stats Sergio pulled from Rides on incidents (see very below).
# My take on Business customer’s liability for ancillary cost caused by a user a.k.a waiving (or limiting the scope of) 3.2 and 6.4:

Ideally of course we should have the end user T&C gap closed before limiting customer's liability. _Until we amend our end user T&C's in the worst case scenario Bolt needs to be ready to pay for any ancillary damage caused by a user._

However the stats provided support the assumption that the risk of any (especially big) loss event is very low. In that light I'd personally understand if the commercial decision is to waive/limit customer’s liability in order to close a major account. For me it would be decisive what would happen in case of big loss events, i.e. health damage caused by a user. 

*Can you confirm my central assumption (based on respective EE law) that also under PT law as* +*for any health damage the damaged party could bypass/disregard any (vague) T&Cs anyway and rely alternatively on*+ +*-tort law-*+ +*non-contractual legal basis instead for making a claim?*+ In my view that would mitigate risk materially making the issue of vague end user T&Cs secondary - the incremental GMV would make up for some minor cost we would struggle recovering from a user until we update the end user T&Cs.

# Should the commercial decision be to limit the scope of customer’s liability to primary fees only then what constitutes _primary_, what _ancillary_ comes down to how it’s defined in the core vertical T&Cs. To be confirmed for PT, but the central direction of travel for _primary fees_ is currently as follows:

* for [Rides|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1wmJv6jt2TLGBZYv6BOHr-NadCxXqTgRngbAOoly24lo/edit] (see 3.8) it’s _fee for services (including for waiting time, tolls, and/or surcharges including a booking fee, municipal tolls, airport surcharges, processing fees for split payments, cancellation fees)_;

Hi César, 

After analysing the issue we have reached the following conclusions:

# The current option not to join the “_Documento de Cálculo de Preço de Viagem_”  to the Taxi T&Cs was an internal Bolt decision. There is no legal provision that obligates us to provide this document separately. Moreover, the T&Cs already state, on clause 5.3. that “_the Trip Price Calculation Document, sent individually to the Operator and forming an_ *_integral part of this Agreement_*_._”. By being an integral part of the T&Cs, there is nothing against being directly attached to the main document itself. 
# If we choose to now start proving the “_Documento de Cálculo de Preço de Viagem_” together with the T&Cs there are some things to consider: 

a) We will have to alter the T&Cs, namely on the provisions that state that the Document is sent separately and individually to each fleet/driver (i.e. this statement is made on the Definitions section of the T&Cs and on Clause 5). 

b) We will have to make this document available to the people registering on the App. It doesn't' necessarily have to be made available to the public but it has to be provided to the new user as he/she accepts the T&Cs during the registration process. The reason for this is that, as the Document is an integral part of the T&Cs, the person registering needs to be conscious of all the terms before accepting (this is a legal obligation coming from article 5.º of DL 446/85, see below). 

!image-20240227-152750.png|width=91.66666666666669%!

c) We should also send a Life Cycle Comm after a fleet is signed up, in order to make sure that the counterpart keeps a version of the contract in a durable format.



*To sum it up:* 

* _Would it be possible to include the "Documento de Cálculo de Preço de Viagem" as an Attachment to the Taxi Operators T&Cs_? Yes, as per above.
* _If we include this document either in the T&C's or the Life Cycle Comms after a fleet is signed up, could we consider that this document is delivered with this method_? We believe the document should be made available to the new user in both formats, first through the T&Cs and then by Life Cycle Comms after registration.
