Hey! Indeed, this question popped up in the last Legal Power Hour. I shared the central insight provided below but advised to reach out via Legal SD to confirm for any specific market whether there are any local considerations I might not be aware of.

From the central end we have confirmed globally (incl with Tax) that in case an order is made under Business payment method then an invoice needs to be issued to the Business customer who has the payment obligation under the Business T&C for the particular order. That is so regardless of the Business payment method - in case of Single invoice as an _aggregated invoice_ [resale strictly for the purposes of VAT laws], in case of Intermediary a _per order invoice_. 

Meaning there is no obligation to share an invoice with an end user who doesn’t have the payment obligation for such orders. And in case of Single invoice trips we already don’t do it because these are issued from provider to Bolt which would be confusing if shared with a customer or user.

For Intermediary I believe we just never stopped sending these as that’s the default for b2c and no harm was found from continuing to send these as trip summaries also to end users despite these being paid by Business. Until now that is, as we have customers who see this as spam. 

From the central end we could stop sending these to end users. Unless we are using these trip summaries to perform a legal obligation to share some compulsory information with the user in particular. I recall that being the case in France I think for Drive vertical when we launched in Lyon for a short period. Overall I believe it should seldom be the case. I doubt Bolt has the obligation to send a “trip summary” as such. But theoretically could be that some information bit included in such trip summary we are unable to share otherwise, i.e. via T&C or app.

Hope that helps!

A.

Hey Sergio,

The invoice depends on what invoicing strategy was set for the fleet. If the invoicing strategy is ‘company based’ commission invoices are issued with fleet’s details. If invoicing strategy is ‘driver based’ each driver would get a separate commission invoice with their own details. Whoever is paying the commission does not really matter for us - but we decide it based on this invoicing strategy. 

For the company you’ve linked, I see it’s “driver based” meaning all drivers would get the monthly invoices in their names. If we change it to company based, there would be one aggregate invoice for all drivers and it would be to fleet’s details.

If you’d like to change a fleet’s invoicing strategy, you’d need to drop a ticket to [https://taxify.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/3/group/61/create/301|https://taxify.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/3/group/61/create/301|smart-link] with fleet ID, and specifying the desired invoicing strategy.

Thanks for the quick response [~accountid:61790cf326a5400071a0c952] so the end goal here is to have driver’s daily balance available as soon as possible the day finishes for the country e.g.

Driver in Thailand (7hours ahead UTC) == 17:00 UTC + a few hours for ingestion lag
Driver in Estonia (2 hours ahead UTC) == 22:00 UTC + a few hours for ingestion lag
Driver in Paraguay (6 hours after UTC) == 06:00 (the next day) UTC + a few hours for ingestion lag

This data will be used externally for downstreaming models used by Finance, Accounting & Controlling to estimate how much $$ we need to allocate to our accounts (e.g. to make sure drivers/partners always get their payouts or spot any issues with liquidity in general) 

As the stakeholders mainly work in Tallinn they would need the up to date balances before they start their day (~9am Tallinn time). Hence we need to run the model after midnight UTC to make sure Europe, Africa, Asia parter balances are there. 

They cannot accept running the model only once e.g. 9am UTC globally because then it may be too late already (e.g. the local time in Thailand is then already 16:00 in the afternoon right). Hence the idea is to fetch as much as possible with one run & then the rest for the Western countries when the data is available. 

Another idea I had is to create a separate DAG (which updates the same model) & pass a country/timezone macro → the main one run 03 UTC for Europe/Africa/Asia & secondary one 09 UTC for America. Would something like this be viable?

I checked the details of how dbt2looker interprets a dbt model. By default, it creates a dimension for every column in the model. If we want any of the columns to become a measure, we have to add additional yml parameters. This is basically duplication of semantics. 

I can offer an alternative logic that would make more use of the semantic layer. This should work great if data marts are constructed from the semantic layer. To create a view out of a data mart:

# In the saved query we specify dimensions and metrics ([example|https://github.com/bolteu/dbt/blob/main/global/models/marts/mart_city_hour_local.yml#L4]) - we can read the metric list from the saved query.
# For each metric in the saved query there is a column in the data mart. All of these columns should become measures in Looker. Default aggregation is SUM, we should be able to manually alter that. 
# All other columns become dimensions (trying to match them from the saved query doesn’t make sense because the names will be changed in the data mart).

What I’m trying to say is that we should probably not add any new data structures that would help define Looker measures, if we can avoid it.

These base fee calculators are set up with the input from local team. They do communicate what commission (and other details such as invoicing strategy) is desired in their market and Billing just sets it up (and this set up is usually approved by OM or CM of the market). So, if there is only a ‘driver based' base fee calculator (which means payouts are going to drivers), that’s because it was requested by the local team this way. 

The reason why payouts are going to drivers is simply because of that. Because the setup was requested to be ‘driver based’. 

Now, there is not really an overwriting when it comes to fee calculators. Base fee calculators are simply default calculators from which Local teams are copying the actual fee calculator of a fleet. So, local team simply chooses this base fee calculator when they onboard a fleet and the settings are copied to this fleet, which can be of course readjusted through a request to Billing.

When it comes to changing the setup, this is quite a common process. Local team would simply need to drop a request to [https://taxify.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/3/group/61/create/301|https://taxify.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/3/group/61/create/301|smart-link] specifying they want to change the invoicing strategy to ‘driver based’. Then we can create a ‘company based’ base fee calculator which would ensure fleets get the payout / monthly invoice. There is no risk from Billing perspective, but since HU is a partner market, I recommend discussing the effects of this with Tax team prior to making that ticket.

Hello!

We checked whether these signups can be caught on the first login, however, sadly *there is not enough unique and repetitive information to form a reject pattern*. Meaning we would not be able to target these accounts without restricting a significant portion of good drivers and accounts. 

However, we did notice some prevention opportunities when these driver accounts as getting activated. It seems that the main duplicate for a lot of these examples is the Certificado DIGITAL de no antecedentes judiciales. Often the verification code (_Código de Verificación_) remains the same while cert numbers (_CON C.I. NRO._) are being manipulated. Hence, if you see this fake/dupe account set up becoming a high-impact and a high-risk issue you may consider an extra check on the documents and compare the online records to what’s stated on the document as well as record the unique numbers presented (to auto-detect duplication). As an example, it is visible for these three with the certificates: 
[+https://admin.bolt.eu/fleet/Drivers/driver/5117300+|https://admin.bolt.eu/fleet/Drivers/driver/5117300]

[https://admin.bolt.eu/fleet/Drivers/driver/5195631|https://admin.bolt.eu/fleet/Drivers/driver/5195631]

[https://admin.bolt.eu/fleet/Drivers/driver/5214149|https://admin.bolt.eu/fleet/Drivers/driver/5214149]

For them to set up these accounts, they need to produce these documents and/or information so if you start being more focused on rejecting these duplicated and manipulated documents then they will also have less opportunity to supply the demand for these accounts and would need to go to great lengths to produce unique and passable (_think also online checks_) information. 

Cheers,

* OfficeConnect for Excel 
* Excel Interface for Planning



----



During refresh of multiple worksheets, WD now display the messages list docked at the bottom of the screen. You can then move the messages list and dock it anywhere on the screen for your convenience. WD uses your last docking position and size to display any future refresh messages.

Hi, [~accountid:61dc710ff63ac80070c15c9d]! Thank you for reaching out. Please find my comments in relation to both of your request:

*Adjust the contracts accordingly*

All our providers (restaurants) are required to accept our General Terms and Conditions (there are a few exceptions for bigger accounts though). General Terms and Conditions is a valid contract concluded between Bolt and the provider. In our [*latest version of General Terms and Conditions*|https://bolt.eu/pl-pl/legal/tnc-bolt-food-partner/?category=delivery] we state the following:

* Clause 5.4 - “*Upon the termination of the Agreement, all rented devices and any other equipment provided by Bolt for using the Bolt Food Platform shall be returned to Bolt* in good order, taking into account the normal wear and tear. Bolt may impose instructions on how to return the devices. *If the Partner fails to return the rented devices and any other equipment, Bolt may impose a contractual penalty in the amount equivalent to the value of the device or keep the deposit if a deposit was applied*”. 
* Clause 12.6 - “The Partner is liable for the loss, theft of or any damage to the rented device provided by Bolt“.

These are explicit contractual obligations undertaken by the provider, which give us the right to charge the provider the full value of the device in case they fail to return it or keep the deposit. There is no need to add these provisions to the Special Terms for these to be effective.



*Have procedure / template of the email that can be used in addressing cases of difficult restaurants*

I would suggest consulting with our product counsels for a global approach regarding this, but this is for the business to decide how you would like to conduct this process of reclaiming money/devices. 

Legally we are able to keep the deposit (if applicable), deduct amount equal to the value of the device from payouts to the provider (due to clause 7.5 of the General Terms and Conditions) or charge the provider for the value of the device by way of an invoice. If such invoice is unpaid the normal procedures of debt collection will apply.

{noformat}%sql
WITH base AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        c.support_case_id,
        c.support_case_created_ts_utc,
        c.support_case_order_id,
        c.support_case_city_id,
        c.support_case_vertical,
        dco.country_name
    FROM core_models_spark.fact_support_case_automation AS a
    INNER JOIN core_models_spark.fact_support_case AS c
        ON c.support_case_id = a.support_case_id 
            AND c.support_case_created_date_utc = a.support_case_created_date_utc 
            AND c.is_support_case_escalated_to_agent
    INNER JOIN customer_support.support_bot_solution_attempt AS b
        ON b.support_case_id = c.support_case_id
            AND b.created_hour >= DATE('2024-01-01')
            AND b.support_case_state_after_successfull_attempt IS NOT NULL
    LEFT JOIN core_models_spark.dim_city AS dci
        ON dci.city_id = c.support_case_city_id
    LEFT JOIN core_models_spark.dim_country AS dco
        ON dco.country_id = dci.country_id
    WHERE a.support_case_created_date_utc >= DATE('2024-01-01')
        AND a.support_case_created_date_utc < DATE('2024-02-01')
        AND a.has_ai_attempt 
),
issues AS (
    SELECT 
        b.support_case_id,
        ARRAY_AGG(i.issue_key) AS issue_keys,
        ARRAY_AGG(s.issue_title) AS issues
    FROM base AS b
    LEFT JOIN ng_customer_support_spark.fact_support_case_issue_keys AS i
        ON i.support_case_id = b.support_case_id
            AND i.issue_created_date >= DATE('2024-01-01')
    LEFT JOIN ng_customer_support_spark.support_issue_store_support_issue AS s
        ON s.issue_key = i.issue_key
    GROUP BY 1
),
case_lang AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        b.support_case_id,
        COALESCE(l.language_set_by_agent, l.detected_language) AS case_language
    FROM base AS b
    LEFT JOIN customer_support.support_case_language_changed AS l
        ON l.support_case_id = b.support_case_id
            AND l.created_hour >= DATE('2024-01-01')
)
SELECT
    b.*,
    l.case_language,
    i.issues,
    i.issue_keys
FROM base AS b
LEFT JOIN issues AS i
    ON i.support_case_id = b.support_case_id
LEFT JOIN case_lang AS l
    ON l.support_case_id = b.support_case_id{noformat}

* If courier continues to keep low AR, courier would get either 14 or 30 days block on the 4th offense

* 6th time courier would get a permament block if his AR was below 40%



We would be checking the count of times courier was caught for having low acceptance rate in the period for the last 6 months, so courier would have a chance to reduce the possible duration of a block in the future, if he was having required acceptance rate for some time.

fyi - the ride-hailing legislation provides the following:

Primary legislation:

Art. 26. -

*At the request of the authorities with powers in the field, provided by this emergency ordinance, the operator of the digital platform or the branch of the non-resident operator of the digital platform, as the case may be, will make available to them all the required information that it holds in relation to the performance of the activity by the operators of alternative transport through the digital platform. The provision of this information is carried out in accordance with the legal provisions in force.*

Art. 29. -

(1) The control of compliance with the provisions of this emergency ordinance is ensured by:

a) Ministry of Communications and Information Society;

b) State Inspectorate for Road Transport Control - I.S.C.T.R.;

*c) National Fiscal Administration Agency*;

*d) agents and police officers designated as traffic policemen within the Romanian Police;*

*e) National Authority for Consumer Protection*;

*f) territorial labour inspectorates*, according to the normative acts that regulate the field of competence of these institutions.

(3) At the headquarters of the operator of the digital platform or of the branch of the non-resident operator of the digital platform in Romania and/or of the alternative transport operator, the control of the alternative transport is carried out by the representatives of the authorities mentioned in para. (1) lit. a) -c), e) and f).



Secondary legislation:

Art. 11. -

The necessary documents for *issuing the technical approval* are:

(...)

# *the representation mandate of the subsidiary ratified by the operator of the digital platform, in which all the rights and obligations conferred on it are mentioned; the right/obligation to make available to public institutions, in accordance with their competences, the data relating to journey, route, passengers, drivers, transport operators, car, location, contracts must be expressly specified.*

Hi Mihai*,*

We are writing in relation to your request dated *19/2/2024.*

We do not have access to, or store your card details when you use Apple Pay. Your device gives a token reference to the card (not the actual card number) to merchants, such as Bolt in this instance, which is issued by the bank during authentication and then used for any payment through Apple Pay.

When you accept an order and it is authorised with Apple Pay, Bolt uses this token to collect payments in the context of the requested service.

In summary, your card number and identity are not shared with Bolt. When you pay, neither Apple nor your device will send your actual card number to merchants such as Bolt.

Please note that payments related to the order are charged according to our Terms and Conditions (Clause 3.1). The Bolt app may begin charging a fare on a waiting time basis.

We ensure that all of our payments are in line with PSD2, acquirer rules and other applicable regulations.

-The providers we use for taking payments are as below:-

* -Adyen N.V. (Netherlands)-
* -Checkout SAS (France)-
* -American Express Payments Europe S.L. (Spain)-

Apple, Inc. (United States) and Google Payment Corp. (United States) are not our providers. We do not have any contractual relationships with either of these providers.

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.

Yours sincerely,
Bolt

There are a few reasons: 

# table schema change. in most cases this actually affects only a small number of columns but because changes in columns are almost impossible, it's often easier to drop the whole table. 
# faulty logic has created extra rows that need to be removed. sometimes this could also be fixed by creating a DELETE FROM ... WHERE ... but there's bigger risk of missing something etc.
# partition key changes. again, it can be done without dropping the table, but in many cases it’s just as painful.

On a positive note: if we need to do the drops, it means we use incremental loading, which is good 😉

Hi [~accountid:712020:0641ea87-e832-482b-8673-ab85e9ad6441] 

Of course. I have been looking at this again following our discussion yesterday and concluded the following:

# Regarding DL 24/2014 about long-distance contracts (that transposes Directive EU 2011/83, which is the consumer protection directive, that Emilie was talking about yesterday), this is +only applicable to contracts with consumers+ - which is not the case here (moreover, there is actually an express exemption in the law, stating that passenger transport service contracts are not under included in the scope of the law. This is the only legal basis that obligates the preservation of the contract in a semi-lasting mean (i.e. email). As this diploma is not applicable, this is not an issue for the matter of the Taxis. 
# I believe that what would be applicable in this case is DL 446/85, which I mentioned below. This is the Law that manages general contractual clauses (which is the case when talking about T&Cs). This law establishes that the terms of the contract must be fully communicated to the new user before acceptation of the T&Cs. This means that what as been done so far, i.e. sending a part of the contract - fee list - only after acceptation is not according to the law. 
# Moreover, DL 7/2004 is applicable to this case as well, for sure. This law establishes that a) all the terms of the contract must be communicated before acceptation (article 32.º) and b) the contract must be sent to the user in order to be kept in a semi-lasting mean (i.e. email) (article 31.º), c) the contract must be signed by the party that is accepting the T&Cs (article 26.º/2). 



So, my suggestion following this analysis is that, once the user as signed in to the platform, provided all the needed documents/data and been accepted to have an active account, the T&Cs (including the "Documento de Cálculo de Preço de Viagem") should be sent via hyperlink. That hyperlink would lead to a space where the user could accept the T&Cs directly. After accepting, the platform would automatically send the signed version to his/hers email account. 

Let me know what you think.
